description:
# Check: upstream editor.test.ts

## Upstream file
tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/editor.test.ts

## Subject
Multi-line text editor: history, autocomplete, word wrapping, kill ring (Emacs-style), undo/redo, mouse, selection, rendering.

## Upstream test count (approx)
173 — the largest upstream file. Expect this check to spawn significant compliance work.

## Behaviors asserted upstream (grouped, enumerate all when checking)

History:
- no-op Up when history empty; shows most recent on Up when editor empty; cycles on repeated Up; returns to empty on Down after browsing; forward nav with Down; exits history on typing; exits on setText; no empty strings; no consecutive duplicates; non-consecutive duplicates allowed; cursor movement vs history when editor has content; limit 100 entries; multi-line entry cursor navigation with Up/Down; navigate from multi-line entry back to newer after cursor movement; (unsaved) marker added/removed/cleared correctly

API:
- returns cursor position; returns lines as defensive copy

Autocomplete:
- splits paragraphs into separate autocomplete requests (marked "not implemented")
- detects start-of-line context; provides path completions; provides command completions; handles item selection; applies completion with proper cursor positioning; trigger character (Tab); filtering and ranking; preview; cancellation with Escape; multiple providers

Enter/submit:
- moves to next line on Enter in multiline mode; single Enter as submit in single-line mode; Ctrl+C cancellation; bracketed paste

Rendering:
- lines with proper syntax highlighting; wide characters (CJK); truncates lines longer than terminal width; wraps long lines at word boundaries; inline code blocks; bold/italic; links; list markers; leading whitespace preservation; mixed languages

Editing:
- undo/redo; cursor position restoration on undo; multi-char undo units for word entry; delete forward and backward; kill ring (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+Y, Alt+Y); rotation and yank-pop; consecutive kill accumulation; backward/forward deletion prepend/append

Theme/keybinding:
- custom theme support; custom keybindings

Layout:
- line number rendering; gutter; column width calculation with wide characters

Selection:
- highlighting (shift+arrow); copy selection (Ctrl+C when selected); delete selection; replace selection with typed character

Mouse:
- cursor positioning; selection; double-click word selection; triple-click line selection; click and drag; shift+click extend

Movement:
- arrows; Ctrl+A; Ctrl+E; Home; End; word boundary (Ctrl+Left/Right, Alt+B/F); page up/down

Delete:
- Delete key; Backspace; Ctrl+W; Alt+D; Ctrl+K; Ctrl+U; forward/backward word deletion behavior relative to kill ring

Special chars:
- backslash as regular character; no overflow with wide CJK/fullwidth text; keeps cursor visible when horizontally scrolling wide text

Kill ring (detailed):
- Ctrl+W/U/K save to kill ring and Ctrl+Y yanks; Ctrl+Y no-op when empty; Alt+Y cycles after Ctrl+Y; Alt+Y no-op without preceding yank; Alt+Y no-op with single entry; consecutive Ctrl+W accumulates; non-delete actions break accumulation; non-yank actions break Alt+Y chain; rotation persists after cycling; backward deletions prepend, forward append; Alt+D saves forward-deleted word; yank in middle; yank-pop in middle

Undo (detailed):
- no-op when empty; coalesces consecutive word chars into one unit; spaces undone one at a time; undoes backspace, forward delete, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+U, yank, paste atomically, Alt+D; cursor movement starts new undo unit

## Upstream dependencies
Editor, CombinedAutocompleteProvider, VirtualTerminal (xterm/headless), defaultEditorTheme, visibleWidth

## Candidate Elixir counterpart(s)
- apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/components/input_test.exs
- apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/interactive_test.exs
- apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/interactive_integration_test.exs
- (possibly a dedicated editor_test.exs if it exists)

## Processing protocol
Same as standard check ticket protocol in epic opi-q5k description. Given the size, the compliance ticket (very likely) may itself need to be split into sub-tickets (history, kill ring, undo, rendering, mouse/selection, etc.) — the processing agent should feel free to split the compliance work into multiple child tickets all blocking opi-q5k.1. Each must require a re-comparison step.
